method: Read all PDF paragraphs 50–109 with surrounding context; existing keyword-based coverage is reassessed, not presumed complete.
phrases: responsible for
having responsibility for causing or dealing with something
对……负责
Who is responsible for checking the report?
谁负责检查这份报告？
Responsibility for the event, not necessarily legal guilt.
a fucking mess
a very confused or badly handled situation, expressed with strong profanity
一团糟（强烈粗口）
The schedule was a complete mess.
日程安排乱成了一团。
Receptive listening target; teaching example deliberately uses the neutral a complete mess. Avoid the source wording in polite/workplace conversation.
follow-up questions
additional questions asked after an initial answer
追问；后续问题
I have two follow-up questions about your proposal.
关于你的提议，我还有两个问题想追问。
Hyphenated adjective follow-up; verb follow up is written separately.
driver's side
the side of a vehicle where the driver sits
驾驶员一侧
The scratch is on the driver's side.
划痕在驾驶员一侧。
Get in means enter the vehicle; paragraph ends without specifying door, so none is added to the quote.
bodily harm
physical injury to a person
身体伤害
The warning mentioned a risk of bodily harm.
警告提到了人身伤害的风险。
Here threatening bodily harm is within a comparison the narrator rejects, not a claim that this happened.
human chain
people standing in a linked line, often as a barrier
人链；人墙
The volunteers formed a human chain.
志愿者们排成了一道人链。
The narrator says it was not like this threatening scenario.
end up getting
eventually obtain or experience something as an outcome
最终得到；最后经历
Did you end up getting the job?
你最后得到那份工作了吗？
Did end up adds emphasis; getting his degree means graduating.
in motion
moving rather than stationary
在移动中
Keep the doors closed while the vehicle is in motion.
车辆行驶时请保持车门关闭。
Formal wording from the notice, paired with restrict a vehicle's ability to move.
overkill
more action or effort than a situation reasonably needs
做得过头；反应过度
Three meetings for this small change would be overkill.
为这个小改动开三次会未免小题大做。
Evaluative figurative noun, not killing; sentence expresses the narrator's judgment.
on their way to
progressing toward a result or destination
即将；正在走向……
They are on their way to finishing the project.
他们快要完成这个项目了。
To is a preposition followed by graduating/finishing, not an infinitive marker.
weighing in
joining a discussion by expressing an opinion
发表看法；参与评论
Several colleagues are weighing in on the proposal.
几位同事正在就这项提议发表看法。
Not body weight; weighing in on a topic is the reusable pattern.
not even in the slightest
not at all, used for strong emphasis
丝毫不；完全不
The delay did not bother her, not even in the slightest.
延误丝毫没有让她烦心。
Parenthetical emphasis interrupts will not ... be; no new proposition is inserted.
segments: chunk:1:there's got to be a better way
There's got to be expresses strong belief that an alternative exists; get out of the parking spot is literal movement, right seeks agreement.
Incident alone missed makes the news and strange conclusion; add those explanatory targets before calling the whole paragraph covered.
Incomplete subject phrase continued by Is the president in 53; no missing words invented.
Read with 52: president is university leader; backed up into and potentially ran over distinguish movement and uncertain injury.
Passive it is decided attributes the responsibility finding; all the student's fault means entirely the student's responsibility, not a narrator-verified finding.
The ones responsible identifies those blamed; they refers to the students, continuing the reported decision.
Long false-start sentence crosses into 57; protests broke out and demanding justice remain barriers beyond introductory phrase matches.
Completes some pretty big scandals from 56. Distinguishes suspension, expulsion and rescinding visas; allegations remain attributed to narration.
Strong profanity intensifies a mess; register and a neutral alternative are explicitly taught.
I guess marks inference; shit responses is a vulgar negative evaluation, related to the register note in 58, not literal waste.
Imagined response in direct-speech style: now we're going to announces the debate series, not a second speaker attribution.
Atrium and university president corrected, but nevertheless is a contrast marker worth teaching; a single matched noun never establishes complete coverage.
A handful of is a small number; end up following describes the outcome. Dislocated students, they is spontaneous speech, not a teaching grammar model.
Footage and that's been released are not explained by the matched negative impression pattern alone.
Continuation contrasts what the footage appears to show; banging on windows means striking them repeatedly, a literal action explained in this decision.
Three simultaneous activities; preventing him from leaving is the previously reviewed prevent + object + from + -ing pattern.
Follow-up questions means additional questions after an answer; target now has a dedicated card.
Gets in means enters the car; source ends at side, so do not fabricate a door phrase.
Back out of the parking spot and so that purpose/result deserve explanation; clear alone is insufficient.
Overall assessment after considering circumstances; not that intense uses that as degree, while I mean is a self-editing filler.
It's not like rejects the imagined threatening scenario; like is also a filler before threatening. Human chain and bodily harm now explicit.
Adds debate topic as context; literal talking about, with no special phrasal-verb meaning.
Brutally punished versus peacefully protesting and gonna be emotions involved need vocabulary/register support; do not erase the contrast.
That is a degree word before volatile. Speaker's impression from footage, not an established factual account.
Apparently signals reported or inferred information; separate reverse motion from alleged foot injury.
Long attributed statement includes ongoing verbal and online abuse and are known to; several word hits do not resolve those barriers.
As well as continues 75; wording resulting in the case of two individual bans is awkward and must not be silently reconstructed from assumed audio.
He says frames the whole list as his account. Followed, surrounded, banged on and shouted describe literal actions rather than separate idioms.
Automatic braking system is a technical phrase needing a card; do not endorse the claimed car behavior or infer automatic driving capabilities.
One-word incredulous reaction to the preceding claim.
Kind of softens the speaker's negative evaluation; crazy is evaluative here, not a diagnosis.
Reported speaker rejects labeling the behavior as protest; past experience is framed by he says.
Motive of silencing speech is an additional collocation/metaphor not covered by the two nouns.
No place in means unacceptable in a community. Opening It is no place is suspect transcript wording; retain and flag instead of repairing a quote.
Did end up emphasizes graduation despite the incident; had his foot run over is a passive experience, not intentional causation.
Senior here means final-year university student, not an elderly person; deserves a contextual card.
Banned from going on campus is prohibition on entry; entire year is duration. Temporal sequence follows graduation, without adding a new timeline.
Gets run over is passive; allegedly scopes the injury claim and president is the university leader.
The notice reads introduces written wording; restricted its ability to maneuver means prevented free movement, and in motion means moving.
Reverse lights illuminated means lights on, not information clarified. Intentional act is what the notice attributes to the student.
All of this seems so overkill is informal evaluative speech; teaching example uses the natural noun predicate would be overkill.
Rhetorical question proposes calling police; so that gives purpose and reverse out means drive backward out of the space.
Question asks motivation; Cornell students restates pedestrians, not a different group.
Expands CUPD and leaves relative clause who work unfinished until 95; acronym and full name are both supplied.
Continues work for Cornell; by default carries an inference about institutional responsibility and needs explanation. Deemed alone is insufficient.
Simple recap of the preceding controversy; earlier this year is relative to recording, not today's date.
Parenthetical emphasis interrupts will not be; caught up in means become involved in trouble. Repeated in is a disfluency retained in source.
File a civil lawsuit and dubbed the Cornell Seven introduce process and naming; Jane Doe is a pseudonym, not a translation of an ordinary name. Need explicit civil/dubbed support.
Gang essayed is euphemistic/ASR wording in this PDF; do not present it as standard English or silently replace it. Dropping out and ripped apart remain useful barriers; all claims are attributed.
While contrasts the complainant's situation with the accused's continued attendance; according to attributes the account. Our lawsuit is retained as printed.
Progress toward graduating, not physical travel; the following -ing form is explicitly taught.
Workshop and reflection papers need educational-context definitions; repeated essays is self-repair, not several separate punishments.
Allegations are claims in the lawsuit; everybody is divided means opinions differ, not literal separation.
Mainstream media and going against need language support. Final Trump is a conversational handoff continued in 105, not part of a repaired quote.
Commenting and fair treatment covered, but prosecutor remains a role-specific gap; do not mark complete just because two phrases match.
Seemingly released and being analyzed indicate uncertain publication and passive analysis; needs dedicated support beyond ordinary text messages.
One accused is a nominal adjective meaning one accused person; stating that continues into 108.
Reverse-role claim is attributed; essayed is the same nonstandard euphemism/possible ASR artifact as 99 and is not an essay-writing vocabulary sense.
Getting doxxed is passive exposure of private information; reviewed word includes meaning and /t/ past-participle ending.
